correctness.rationale: The fixed unweighted degree-normalized generator gives exact directional derivatives on right-only indicator cuts: (s/q)W-(1+2s/q)C(Y), with all such derivatives controlled by the q singleton columns (q+2)(a_j+b_j)>=W. For cuts containing u and a right set Y of size s, Phi=|d_s|B-(1+d_s)A+sum_{j in Y}tau_j(s), with d_s=1/2-s/q and tau_j(s)=(1+d_s+|d_s|)a_j-(1-d_s+|d_s|)b_j. Sorting maximizes the fixed-s derivative; taking complements exhausts the cuts. Each indicator has exact first-order Euler variation for eps<1/2; coarea of nested superlevels and triangle inequality extend contraction to all real functions and the Euler exponential limit to all t>=0. Any positive derivative yields small-t violation. Independently evaluated direct cut derivatives and the sorting test for 85 positive integer weight profiles with 1<=q<=5. For q=3, (a,b)=((4,1,1),(1,8,8)) has all singleton derivatives negative but Phi({u,y1})=1/6 and J=3. Finite checks corroborate, not prove the infinite classification.

value.rationale: The family K_{2,q} transitions at q=3 from path/cycle to a genuine multicycle graph. Exact arbitrarily anisotropic variation-weight criteria and the first mixed-cut obstruction identify a natural failure of local certificates. The sorted test avoids enumerating exponentially many cuts; its q² log q complexity and constructive counterexample are mathematical structural information, not a trivial instance of coarea.

final_claim: For q>=3, normalized Markov heat on K_{2,q} contracts every positive independently edge-weighted graph-total-variation seminorm on all real signals at all nonnegative times exactly when q column inequalities and q+1 top-s sorted mixed-cut inequalities hold, with an O(q^2 log q) decision test and a sharp five-vertex counterexample to singleton-only tests.
limitations: q>=3, positive variation weights, unweighted normalized heat, real signals only; no weighted jump rates or general K_pq.
